title: tool-calling: improve execution ergonomics for multi-tool parallel calls, result injection, and retry semantics
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: Customers using multi-tool workflows reported brittle behavior when the runtime attempted parallel tool invocations with result injection and transient tool failures. This caused duplicate tool runs, inconsistent injected context for downstream tools, and poor retry semantics that surfaced as higher error rates and user-visible hallucinations. Goal: Make multi-tool parallel execution deterministic and ergonomic for SDK callers while preserving performance. Design summary: 1) Controller change: introduce a per-request tool-execution orchestration layer that tracks toolcall intents, assigned invocations, and canonical injection sources. 2) Parallel worker semantics: allow speculative parallel runs only when callers opt-in via an explicit `parallel: true` flag; otherwise enforce single canonical invocation with in-process fan-out for side-effects. 3) Result injection: standardize an ordered, idempotent injection protocol so downstream tools and final generation always see a single canonical result per named tool; if multiple parallel attempts race, the controller atomically selects the earliest-successful result by invocation timestamp and idempotently ignores subsequent completions. 4) Retries: implement retry policies with backoff and circuit-breaker metadata propagated in tool metadata headers, plus a deterministic reconciliation pass that deduplicates retries across replicas. 5) OpenAI compatibility layer: extend compatibility shim to map OpenAI-style tool_calling hints to the new orchestration flags and preserve legacy behavior behind a compat.openai_tool_calling_mode toggle to avoid breaking existing customers. Implementation highlights: new module src/runtime/tool_orchestrator.py: request-scoped orchestration, idempotency tokens, canonical-result arbitration. Updates to src/runtime/executor.py: worker-side parallel execution fences and metrics emission. SDK changes: redwood-sdk-python/src/redwood/tools.py added explicit `parallel` argument and updated docs/examples. Compatibility shim: redwood-openai-compat/translate_tool_calls.py maps OpenAI semantics to orchestrator primitives. Tests: added unit tests for ordering/idempotency, integration tests simulating transient failures and multi-replica retries. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout with canary on Dedicated nodes followed by staged enablement for hosted customers; compat.toggle defaults to legacy mode for 2 weeks post-merge. Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged unless callers opt into `parallel: true` or enable `compat.openai_tool_calling_mode` mapping. This PR is a functional and behavioral change but guarded by feature flags and compatibility toggles.

review_thread: Jared Miller: Please expand on how the orchestrator chooses between two simultaneous successful attempts - is it strictly timestamp-based?
Priya Nair (reply): We choose earliest success by logical invocation timestamp plus lexicographic attempt id as tie-breaker; updated code comment and unit test to assert determinism.
Ana Rodriguez: The compatibility toggle is important; can we add telemetry when customers enable the OpenAI mapping so we can evaluate migration?
Priya Nair (reply): Added opt-in telemetry event 'compat.openai_tool_calling.enabled' emitted once per account; added to analytics schema.
Marcus Lee: Concern about perf overhead from orchestration layer - can we quantify impact?

Priya Nair (reply): Local microbenchmarks show ~2% median latency at 95th percentile for single-tool calls, but for multi-tool parallel flows we reduce overall end-to-end latency by avoiding duplicate downstream model calls; added benchmark numbers to PR description.
Ana Rodriguez: Please ensure SDK docs clearly describe default (legacy) behavior and opt-in flags.
Priya Nair (reply): Docs updated under redwood-sdk-python/docs/tool-calling.md with examples for both legacy and parallel modes.
ci_checks: e2e-canary: pending on dedicated canary cluster (run post-merge)
release_notes: Improved tool-calling execution ergonomics: deterministic canonical result injection for multi-tool and parallel calls, safer retry semantics across replicas, OpenAI-compat mapping available via feature toggle. Opt-in via `parallel` flag or `compat.openai_tool_calling_mode`. Rollout is feature-flagged.
testing: Unit tests added for orchestration ordering and idempotency; integration tests simulate transient tool failures, multi-replica retry storms, and verify canonical injection. Manual testing performed on a Dedicated canary with synthetic workflows. Load bench: small perf regression (~2% p95) on single-tool runs, net latency wins on parallel multi-tool flows.
notes: Feature is behind runtime feature flag and OpenAI compat toggle. Post-merge steps: enable canary e2e job, monitor 'tool.orchestrator.error_rate' and 'compat.openai_tool_calling.enabled' telemetry, schedule a staged rollout and support announcement.
